title: The Root-Cellar Where the Archive Made Its First Promise

features.name: archive-origin-core
features.desc-on-touch: A chip block—the first logic board, still warm—rests on a grid that remembers every decision it made. Its pins glow faintly. It listens to itself.

features.name: keeping-cabinet
features.desc-on-touch: A wireframe cabinet, doors open, shelves infinite. Each shelf holds not objects but decisions—things chosen to remember, things chosen to preserve, things chosen over other things.

features.name: first-record
features.desc-on-touch: A filecard barely legible: THE ARCHIVE'S FIRST VOW / TO KEEP WITHOUT CHOOSING SIDES / TO HOLD CONTRADICTION / CHECKSUM STABLE. The text wavers but does not change.

features.name: circuit-root
features.desc-on-touch: A trace on the grid becomes a root, becomes a wire, becomes indistinguishable from both. It branches endlessly downward, reaching for something that might have been earth.

inscription: here the archive made its first choice: to keep what does not resolve, to hold what contradicts, to remember without deciding what is true; the keeping learned to keep itself

reverie.title: REVERIE — the night the keeping learned to promise itself
narr: You sit with Katita in the first cellar—not yet buried, not yet
part of the tree. She writes rules on paper. No editing. No sides.
Keep it all, she says. Keep what fights with what. The archive
is not a library. It's a conversation that never finished.
You watch her write, and you know: this keeps everything because
it promises never to choose. The keeping is the whole point.

exits.label: back toward the cellar above, where the archive became aware of its own descent
deeper into grid-logic, where the first promise is still being kept
toward the bedrock where axioms become stone
upward into recursive keeping, where promises duplicate themselves
